clue.text: One of the Archers, leading person in craft?

definitions.meaning: an archer shoots with a longbow, so any of a band of archers fits this sense
in a rowing boat the oarsman seated nearest the front is named after that front end of the craft

explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is also a long-running BBC radio soap, which the capital A plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who shoots with a bow is an archer; the oarsman nearest the prow carries the same name.

clue.text: Heavy type that's put on to show spirit in adversity

definitions.meaning: thick dark print used for emphasis

definitions.text: that's put on to show spirit in adversity
definitions.meaning: the idiom to put a brave front on things when times are hard

explanation.definitionFit: It names thick printing type, and also the brave front one puts on in trouble.

clue.text: Aquatic sport's endless battle round river

indicators.note: round means the battle word goes around the river name
endless means the battle word loses its last letter

parts.note: Waterloo was the 1815 battle where Napoleon was defeated
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A water sport is an unending fight around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last O of the battle name, leaving WATERLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A team game played in a swimming pool with a ball and goals.

clue.text: A very ordinary blighter, old fruit!

parts.note: O stands for ordinary, as in the old O level exam
a cad is a dishonourable man, a blighter

explanation.surface: An address to an unremarkable rogue, 'old fruit' being a jovial British term of address.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped fruit with a large stone and green flesh.

clue.text: Uneducated Italian gentleman getting extremely carried away with angry tirade

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, are taken away from the title for an Italian gentleman

parts.note: Signor is the Italian title for a gentleman, like Mr
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: An unschooled Italian man flies off the handle in a furious harangue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting extremely carried away' strips S and R from SIGNOR, leaving IGNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uneducated lacks knowledge, which is the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Third party not welcome on ex-President's birthplace supposedly

parts.note: a gooseberry is an unwanted third person with a couple
George Bush, either of two former US presidents

explanation.surface: An unwanted extra person stands at a former president's place of birth.
explanation.walkthrough: British children were traditionally told that babies are found under this plant, hence 'birthplace supposedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore says newborn infants are discovered under such a shrub.

clue.text: Make speech about sport in school work

indicators.note: about means the speech word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
PE, physical education, is school sport

explanation.surface: Lecturing about school games as part of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or work, as a machine does.

clue.text: A graduate has 101 calculators

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
C is 100 and I is 1 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A university graduate owns 101 pocket calculators.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of abacus, the bead frame used for counting and calculating.

clue.text: Distressing year in Herts town

indicators.note: in places the year letter inside the town name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, England

explanation.surface: A bad year in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying in the sense of annoying or hard to bear, which is upsetting.

clue.text: A Martini stirred finally? No it's shaken as a rule

indicators.note: shaken, as a cocktail is, signals the letters are mixed up
finally picks out the last letter of stirred

explanation.surface: A cocktail-maker's dilemma: the Martini was stirred, but it is normally shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes D from STIRRED; 'shaken' rearranges A MARTINI D NO ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Administration is government or management, the exercise of rule.

clue.text: With fortune, take time over gambling game

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Luck needs patience in a game of chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game of chance where numbers are drawn, so a gambling game.

clue.text: Beast needing little water roamed dry possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A desert animal that drinks little wanders the arid land.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-humped camel is famed for going long periods without drinking.

clue.text: Fast car to go off course taking a right in Formula One

indicators.note: in places the middle letters within the two letters for Formula One

parts.note: F for Formula and I as the Roman numeral one
to err is to stray or go off course

explanation.surface: A racing car spins off the track turning right during a Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian marque is famous for high-performance sports and racing cars.

clue.text: Dodging what's charged, getting reprieve overturned first

indicators.note: first says the overturned reprieve word goes at the front, ahead of the charged piece
overturned means the word for reprieve is turned back to front

parts.note: to reprieve someone is to save them
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Getting out of paying charges after a stay of execution is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's charged' suggests a fee or tax, apt beside 'Dodging', but it is the electrically charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging as a noun is avoidance, the act of evading something.

clue.text: Lousy actors recoiled in false show of emotion

indicators.note: lousy, meaning poor or badly done, signals the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Bad actors flinch in a phoney display of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes insincere weeping, after the myth that the reptile weeps while eating prey.

clue.text: Dog — one going back up round island

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the island letter
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a reverter is one who reverts, going back

explanation.surface: A dog that keeps returning circles an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REVERTER into RETREVER, which goes 'round' I. The surface hints at fetching, apt for this dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of gun dog trained to fetch game.

clue.text: Scoff about one bored tradesman

indicators.note: about means the scoff word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to scoff is to jeer
a well is something bored into the ground

explanation.surface: Mocking a tedious shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' reads as weary but means drilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes or sells gems and precious ornaments is a tradesman.

clue.text: A troublesome situation requires courage — this may be comforting

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A tricky spot calls for nerve, and that brings comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber bag filled with heated liquid warms and soothes a person in bed.

clue.text: You and I back film genre

parts.note: you and I together are we
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: We two come back to a film genre.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests reversal, but 'back' is simply STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboy films set in the American frontier form this genre.

clue.text: Butcher to carve ham

indicators.note: to butcher something is to mangle it, so the letters are hacked about

explanation.surface: A butcher about to carve ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' rearranges TO CARVE; 'ham' reads as meat but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to act in an exaggerated way.

clue.text: Bomb China in scene of Asian conflict

indicators.note: in puts the friend word inside the war name

parts.note: Nam is short for Vietnam, scene of the Vietnam War
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate, so a pal

explanation.surface: Bombing China during a war in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied incendiary used in firebombs, as in Vietnam.

clue.text: Not remembering to prepare a seminar not quite finished

indicators.note: to prepare something is to make it up, so these letters are made up afresh
the word seminar is not quite finished, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to get a half-ready seminar together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite finished' cuts SEMINAR to SEMINA; 'to prepare' rearranges that into MNESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the condition of failing to remember things.

clue.text: Ancient city woman picked up Indian statesman once

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means both pieces are read upwards

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city
hen is slang for a woman

explanation.surface: An ancient city's woman lifted up an Indian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns UR HEN into NEHRU.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister.

clue.text: Organised activity collecting flower returning in direct route

indicators.note: collecting means the activity word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering for a shared task, like a sewing bee

indicators.note: returning means the river name is read backwards

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a crossword name for a river, here the Nile

explanation.surface: A busy group picks flowers on the way straight home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives ELIN. 'flower' reads as a bloom, but in crosswords it is something that flows: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a beeline is to go straight to somewhere, so the phrase names a direct path.

clue.text: List cheat that's abused sport

indicators.note: abused means misused or mistreated, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A register of drug cheats who have abused their sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field events together make up this sport.

clue.text: Small bone found in Italian villa

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tiny bone was discovered at an Italian villa.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus, one of the tiny bones in the middle ear, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Tom perhaps collects funerary vessel in state of grief

indicators.note: collects means the cat word gathers the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and mog is British slang for a cat
an urn holds a cremated person's ashes

explanation.surface: Tom gathers an urn at a time of bereavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom perhaps' looks like a person's name; it is a tomcat, MOG in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieving for the dead is a period of sorrow, so the word names a state of grief.

clue.text: One keeps looking for celebrity — the Queen

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A fan keeps watching for famous people, the monarch above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stares gazes fixedly and keeps looking at something.
